title: a native pin given more than one argument is rejected at the call: the pin takes exactly one reference to a function declared in this project
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (Locked), spells the provisional candidate as `native(checksum)` — one reference — and the same page makes the pin 'a checked assertion'. docs/DECISIONS.md, 'TypeScript and native classification' (Locked), repeats it. An extra argument is not a second pin and not a modifier; it is a call the compiler has no reading for, and the fail-open is quiet: an implementation that takes `node.arguments[0]` and ignores the rest pins the first function and discards the rest of the author's text without saying so. This is the SECOND BRANCH of SMITHERS3005 and it is written as its own case on purpose. The two branches have different positions — the unresolvable-subject branch reports at the ARGUMENT (21-native-pin/a-pin-whose-argument-is-not-a-project-function-is-rejected, 9:8) and this one reports at the CALL — so a single case would have pinned one branch and left the other free, which is how a backend comes to own half of a code. No `messageContains` is declared. The two backends legitimately word this diagnostic differently — measured on SMITHERS1503, where the reference says "only as an expression statement or direct return" and the fork says "only as an expression statement or a direct return" — and conformance/README.md reserves `messageContains` for rules whose PAYLOAD is the promise, which here it is not: the code and the authored position are the whole contract, and a fragment of the sentence around them would be a wording assertion wearing a contract's clothes. Note what is NOT declared: no TypeScript arity diagnostic appears, because `native` is a compiler-owned binding from `smithers:native` and the refusal is the language's own, reported before any stock check of the emitted module set could run. Both backends refuse it today, so this case pins current behaviour on both rather than reproducing a live one-sided defect.
